# Architecture

The profile dictates the layers and the direction of imports. A file that fits no layer is a signal: stop and ask.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Profile `spa-feature`

Vite single-page application, one directory per use case, imports flowing strictly downwards.

### When this profile fits

- The interface talks to an HTTP API that already exists or is being built alongside it.
- The team is small enough for one repository and one deployment unit.
- Screens are composed of a handful of independent use cases.

### When it does not

- The product needs server-side rendering or streaming for SEO or first paint.
- Several teams own separate parts of the same interface and deploy independently.
- The application is mostly static content with little interaction.

### Layers

| Layer | Path | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | `src/app` | `features`, `entities`, `shared` |
| `features` | `src/features/*` | `entities`, `shared` |
| `entities` | `src/entities/*` | `shared` |
| `shared` | `src/shared` | nothing |

### Rules

- **SPA-001** · `eslint-boundaries` — Every use case is a directory under `src/features/` holding `ui/`, `model/`, `api/` and an `index.ts` that is its only public entry point.
  Why: A feature that can be read, moved or deleted on its own is what keeps a growing interface understandable.
- **SPA-002** · `eslint-boundaries` — A feature never imports another feature; two features are composed in `app/`.
  Why: Cross-imports between features are how a modular interface silently becomes one block.
- **SPA-003** · `eslint-boundaries` — Only the public index of a layer is imported; reaching into a feature's internal files is forbidden.
  Why: Without a public surface, every internal rename becomes a breaking change for the whole app.
- **SPA-004** · `eslint-boundaries` — `shared/` contains nothing that names the business domain: no entity type, no feature name, no endpoint.
  Why: The day business vocabulary enters `shared/`, everything depends on everything again.
- **SPA-005** · guidance — An entity under `src/entities/` holds the shape of a domain object, its zod schema and its display components, and no use case.
  Why: Two features displaying the same object must show it the same way without depending on each other.
- **SPA-006** · `eslint-boundaries` — A feature never imports from `app/`; composition flows one way only.
  Why: The reverse import is what makes a feature impossible to reuse on another screen.
- **SPA-007** · guidance — Routes are declared in `src/app`, and each route loads its feature lazily.
  Why: The routing map stays readable in one file and the first bundle stays small.
- **SPA-008** · `dependency-cruiser` — The dependency graph has no cycle and no orphan module.
  Why: A cycle breaks lazy loading and tree-shaking; an orphan is dead code nobody dares delete.
- **SPA-012** · `eslint-boundaries` — A new feature is created with its `index.ts` in the first commit; a feature without a public index does not exist for the rest of the application.
  Why: The index is where the author decides what is public, before anyone depends on the rest.

### Anti-patterns

- **SPA-AP-001** · `eslint-boundaries` — A `src/utils/` directory collecting whatever fits nowhere else.
  Why: It becomes a dependency of every layer and belongs to none.
  Instead: Put the function in `shared/lib` under a name that says what it does, or inside the only feature that uses it.
- **SPA-AP-002** · `eslint-boundaries` — Importing `../../features/notes/model/useNotes` to reuse a hook.
  Why: The importing feature now breaks whenever the other one reorganises its internals.
  Instead: Export the hook from the feature index if it is public, otherwise move the shared logic down to `entities/` or `shared/`.

### Reference example

The `notes` feature: a paginated list with its three states, a validated creation form and a detail view.

Files:

- `src/entities/note/model/note.ts`
- `src/entities/note/ui/NoteCard.tsx`
- `src/features/notes/api/notesApi.ts`
- `src/features/notes/model/useNotes.ts`
- `src/features/notes/ui/NoteList.tsx`
- `src/features/notes/ui/NoteForm.tsx`
- `src/features/notes/index.ts`
- `src/app/routes.tsx`

Rules illustrated: **SPA-001**, **SPA-002**, **SPA-003**, **CORE-010**, **CORE-040**, **CORE-050**, **CORE-060**

### Dependencies

**Allowed without discussion**

| Artifact | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `react-router` | Routing and lazy loading of the screens declared in `app/`. |
| `zod` | Validation of everything that enters the application, and inference of the matching types. |
| `class-variance-authority` | Component variants declared next to the component, on top of the tokens. |
| `@radix-ui/react-*` | Accessible primitives for dialogs, menus and popovers, styled with the project tokens. |

**Forbidden**

| Artifact | Rationale |
|---|---|
| `moment` | Unmaintained and heavy; `Intl` and the native date API cover the need. |
| `lodash` | The whole library for two helpers; the language now has them. |
| `axios` | `fetch` plus the api layer already give typed calls and error handling. |

**Procedure to add a dependency**

1. Check that neither the standard library nor an already allowed dependency covers the need.
2. Propose the dependency, its purpose and its weight in the bundle, then wait for confirmation.
3. Add it in its own commit (`build(deps)`) touching only `package.json` and the lockfile.
4. Record it in `docs/adr/` when it changes how a layer is written.

## Option `state-context`

Client state is shared through React contexts, one per concern.

### Rules

- **CTX-001** · guidance — One provider per concern, declared by the feature that owns the state, never a single global provider.
  Why: A global provider re-renders the whole tree and belongs to nobody.
- **CTX-002** · guidance — A context carries a value that changes rarely; frequently changing values stay in local state.
  Why: Every context update re-renders all its consumers, whatever they use from it.
